tweets.text:
The safest borrowers on earth are getting expensive to lend to.

The spread on hyperscaler bonds, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Oracle and SpaceX, blew out to 1.3 points over Treasurys, nearly double the 0.75 on the broad investment-grade index. Goldman sees $400 billion of new hyperscaler debt in 2027, on top of $250 billion this year.

The AI buildout is getting financed in the bond market, and the flood is repricing even AAA credit. Alphabet already has bonds maturing in 2075 that yield 6.5%. Reach for that in a long-duration fund and you own a 40-year bet on a business nobody can forecast, right as the long end reprices. The compensation has moved to short-dated and data-center bonds. Fifty-year Big Tech paper is where the duration risk hides now.

$LQD

The 60/40 portfolio is dying and Washington is holding the knife.

Federal debt sits at 99% of GDP today. CBO projects 175% by 2056.

Stock-bond correlation already flipped positive. Gold and real assets are doing the job bonds used to do but the extra volatility makes a lot of investors’ stomach churn.

The hottest emerging market story is losing its bid.

India's IPO proceeds are down about 20% this year, $5.78 billion raised versus $7.32 billion a year ago, after back-to-back record hauls of $22 billion in 2025 and $21 billion in 2024.

Issuers are slashing deal sizes to get anything done. Manipal Health cut its raise, Indo-MIM went from a $700 million target to $396 million, and Juniper Green nearly halved its offering.

Foreign buyers have pulled back, so local institutions set the price now, and they are paying less. When the market everyone loved cannot float deals at the valuations it wants, the speculative tide is going out.

$INDA
